The Widow of Nain
NAY-in
noun phrase
From the place-name Nain, a city of Galilee, where Christ raised the only son of a widow from the dead.

Biblical Definition

As Christ drew near the gate of the city called Nain, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and much people of the city was with her (Luk 7:12). Beholding the desolation of a woman bereft of husband and now of her only son, when the Lord saw her, He had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not (Luk 7:13). Then He came and touched the bier, and the bearers stood still; and He said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise. And he that was dead sat up, and began to speak; and He delivered him to his mother (Luk 7:14; Luk 7:15). The dictionary marks the raising at Nain as the first of Christ’s raisings of the dead, and the purest display of His unbidden compassion: no man asked Him, no faith was named, but His own mercy moved Him toward a weeping widow. There came a fear on all, and they glorified God, saying, That God hath visited His people (Luk 7:16). So the Scripture teaches the divine power of Christ over death itself, who needed but a word to call the dead to life; and it sets forth the tenderness of the Lord, who turns the funeral into a resurrection, a pledge of that day when He shall call all His own from the grave by the same almighty voice.

Webster 1828 Definition

A widow of Nain whose only son Christ raised from the dead out of His own unbidden compassion.

THE WIDOW OF NAIN, whose only son Christ raised from the dead.

Her dead son was carried out at the city gate, much people with her.

The Lord saw her, had compassion, and said unto her, Weep not.

He touched the bier and said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise.

The dead man sat up and spake, and He delivered him to his mother.

Key Scripture

Luk 7:12 — "Now when he came nigh to the gate of the city, behold, there was a dead man carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow: and much people of the city was with her."

Luk 7:13 — "And when the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her, and said unto her, Weep not."

Luk 7:14 — "And he came and touched the bier: and they that bare him stood still. And he said, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise."

Luk 7:16 — "And there came a fear on all: and they glorified God, saying, That a great prophet is risen up among us; and, That God hath visited his people."

Modern Corruption

A miracle of Christ; the raising at Nain shews His compassion on the mourner and His divine power over death.

expand to see more

The raising of the widow’s son at Nain has drawn little redefinition from the present age, surviving as one of the three recorded raisings of the dead by Christ. The dictionary records it that the reader may mark the tenderness of the Lord toward a desolate widow and the almighty power that called her son from death by a word.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the divine compassion and resurrection power of Christ. None asked Him and no faith was named; His own mercy was moved toward the weeping widow, and He turned her funeral into a resurrection. So the dictionary draws the sign: He who said to the dead, Young man, I say unto thee, Arise, is the Lord of life, and this raising is a pledge of the last day, when He shall call all His own from the grave by the same voice. The mourner is taught to look not to a great prophet only, but to God who hath visited His people in the person of His Son.

Usage

"Like the widow of Nain, the mourner finds in Christ a Lord moved with compassion."

"Young man, I say unto thee, Arise, is the word of Him who is Lord over death."

"His raisings are a pledge that He shall call all His own from the grave."
